title: Predictive reserved warm‑up and temporary allocation for scheduled traffic spikes
creator: Claire Hu
description:
Background: Reserved customers occasionally run predictable, scheduled campaigns (e.g., product launches, marketing blasts, Black Friday regional promos) that cause short-lived but large increases in inference throughput. Today we rely on manual capacity top‑ups or burst buffers that either require long lead time or lead to overprovisioning and unexpected billing complexity.

Goal: Implement a safe, auditable "warm‑up" flow that pre‑allocates temporary quota / burst units for reserved customers ahead of known scheduled spikes and automatically reconciles usage with detailed ledger entries. The system should: 1) allow customers (via Console or API) and Redwood SRE to register a scheduled spike window; 2) predict a conservative pre‑allocation amount using historical patterns and explicit customer inputs; 3) provision temporary reservations from a global burst pool or from a customer's reserved commit (with configurable policy); 4) produce immutable ledger entries and reconciliation adjustments to ensure billing correctness and explainability; 5) expire and reconcile allocations post‑window with automated refunds/crediting where appropriate.
proposal_summary: We will introduce a scheduled‑allocation service that integrates with existing quota manager and ledger. It will compute a warm‑up allocation (two possible modes: conservative predictive mode using recent 90/30 day heuristics, or explicit requested mode where the customer provides an expected peak). Allocations can be sourced from: a) the tenant's reserved quota (temporary reallocation of commit), b) a shared burst pool with priority tiers, or c) a paid short‑term quota addenda. Allocations are timeboxed, idempotent, and tied to a signed customer manifest to support audit and disputes.
design_decisions: Use a separate scheduled_allocation object in the quota service rather than mutating tenant quota directly to make rollbacks safe
Emit preallocation and reconciliation events into the existing billing ledgers so all changes are auditable and retriable
Conservative predictive default: min(2x recent rolling 24h 95th percentile, explicit customer declared peak) capped by policy per‑tenant and global safeguards
Fallback behavior: if preallocation fails, route traffic to lower‑cost model variants and emit a customer alert via console and webhook
acceptance_criteria: Customers can create a scheduled spike entry in Console and via the new API endpoint /v1/quotas/scheduled_allocations
System computes a proposed warmup allocation and shows an estimated cost/impact before customer confirmation
Reserved customers who opt in receive a pre‑allocation in the scheduled window and requests are allowed up to the temporary allocation without throttling
All allocation and reconciliation changes produce ledger entries with metadata: allocation_id, source (reserved|burst_pool|paid), start_ts, end_ts, predicted_peak, actual_usage
Post‑window automated reconciliation runs within 30 minutes and issues credits/refunds when actual usage < preallocated units or bills for overage when usage > preallocation per policy
Telemetry dashboards show per‑allocation success/failure, reconciliation delta, and customer visible audit log entry
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (internal alpha): implement service behind feature flag, expose API for SRE/customer success to create allocations manually for a handful of pilot tenants. Phase 2 (beta): surface in Console, enable predictive heuristics, open to self‑serve for reserved customers. Phase 3: GA with guardrails and paid addenda flows. Each phase will include metrics, alerting, and a rollback plan (revoke allocations and reconcile).
testing_plan: Unit tests for allocation computation and ledger writes; integration test that simulates a scheduled window end and verifies reconciliation; chaos test where allocation source fails and system routes to fallback models; billing e2e with synthetic invoices and customer dispute simulation. Use a canary group of 5 tenants for live validation for Phase 1.
migration_and_backcompat: Scheduled allocations are additive; if the service is rolled back, allocations created during the rollback window will be honoured by the ledger but no new allocations will be accepted. Existing quota semantics remain untouched for tenants that do not opt in. Migration notes include a one‑time backfill job to emit allocation artifacts for pilot customers to ensure downstream analytics picks them up.
security_and_compliance_notes: All scheduled allocation manifests will be stored with tenant context and immutability flags for 7 years for auditability. Sensitive payment adjustments will follow existing billing PCI/HSM processes. We will add RBAC controls so only authorized SRE/CS/tenant admins can create allocations. Request to confirm with Security that retention policy and ledger immutability meets enterprise audit requirements.
risks_and_mitigation: Over‑provisioning leads to increased short‑term costs — mitigate with conservative default and soft caps, require explicit confirmation for high cost allocations
Allocation bookkeeping bugs could cause double‑billing — mitigate by writing allocation intents as first class ledger records and requiring reconciliation to be idempotent
Burst pool starvation during concurrent spikes — mitigate with priority tiers and emergency throttles plus automated fallback routing to cheaper models
